clue.text: Dance workers in trousers that stretch

parts.note: to skip is to move in a light dancing step
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Dancers employed in some show are wearing elastic trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting elasticated trousers, often with a strap under the foot, worn for fashion as well as skiing.

clue.text: Born in crowd, raised in Belfast threesome

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the second, so one sits within the other
in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pack is a crowd or throng of people
née, used before a maiden name, means born

explanation.surface: Someone born in a crowd and brought up in Belfast belongs to a group of three.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed crowd word KCAP is split by the birth word to give K-NEE-CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneecap is an Irish-language hip-hop trio from Belfast, three performers who made the band famous.

clue.text: Passable cuts for every card game

indicators.note: one word cuts into the other, splitting it open around itself

parts.note: per means for each or for every
OK means acceptable or passable

explanation.surface: A mediocre set of cuts dealt out for every round of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a gambling game played with a standard pack, built on betting over hands.

clue.text: One rebuilt casino invests divided capital

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one word wraps round another
something rebuilt is put together again in a different form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A redeveloped casino puts money into a city split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invests' plays on its financial sense to suit the casino, but here it means surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia, capital of Cyprus, has been partitioned between Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides since 1974 by a buffer zone.

clue.text: Two Frenchmen battling with Interpol as in The Saint

indicators.note: things battling are thrown about in a struggle, so their letters end up jumbled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of monsieur, so two of them give MM
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of French criminals fight the police, a plot straight out of a TV thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Templar is the gentleman adventurer of Leslie Charteris's novels, nicknamed The Saint and played on television by Roger Moore.

clue.text: Poor grades blocking musical trainees

indicators.note: the grades block the middle of the show title, sitting inside it like an obstruction

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
D and E are low exam grades

explanation.surface: Students in a stage school are let down by bad marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets are young people training for the armed forces or police, so they are trainees in uniform.

clue.text: More tea houses where Kings Road is located

indicators.note: used as a verb, houses means holds inside, so the drink encloses the other word

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
else means more or additional, as in anything else

explanation.surface: Extra cafés open along a fashionable London shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a noun about buildings on the street but is the verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: The King's Road is the famous shopping street running through the Chelsea district of west London.

clue.text: Director-General moved fast to cover lives stigmatised

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so the abbreviation wraps the short word

parts.note: DG is the standard abbreviation for Director-General
is means exists or lives
to race is to move fast

explanation.surface: A broadcasting chief hurried to hush up lives that had been tarnished by scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disgraced has lost respect and is marked with shame, the same as being branded or stigmatised.

clue.text: See 5
Magistrate miserable having released 50

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: bleak means cheerless or miserable
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A gloomy judge has just let off fifty defendants.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is old British slang for a magistrate or judge.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a beak is a magistrate, or a schoolmaster, an informal term for someone in authority.

clue.text: Issue consuming Brown small, or hard to handle?

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one word swallows the others inside it

parts.note: to come forth is to issue or emerge
umber is a brown earth pigment
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A question about whether a little Brown, perhaps Gordon, is awkward to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cumbersome is bulky and unwieldy, awkward to carry or manage because of its size or weight.

clue.text: Flyer downed in nice warm gust — wings always failing

indicators.note: the wings of each word are its outer edges, and these fail every time, leaving only the insides

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An aviator is brought down in a pleasant warm breeze because the aircraft's wings keep breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the myth: the wings fail and the flyer falls, which is also the instruction to strip each word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wings of feathers and wax, went too near the sun, and plunged into the sea.

clue.text: Tunnels side by side near the bridge?

definitions.text: Tunnels side by side near the bridge?

parts.words: Tunnels side by side near the bridge?
parts.note: surface reading: twin road or rail tunnels running parallel next to a river crossing; setter's reading: the bridge of the nose, with two air passages just below it

explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is part of the face, not a river crossing; the paired tunnels are the two openings at the base of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The two nasal openings are parallel passages for air lying just below the bony ridge at the top of the face.

clue.text: Shock a mate unnamed in US region

indicators.note: unnamed means without a name, and N is the abbreviation of name, so that letter goes

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
taken as written
china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so a china is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone stuns an anonymous friend while travelling through part of America.
explanation.walkthrough: Mate = CHINA comes from Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate); removing N for name leaves CHIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalachia is the mountainous cultural region of the eastern United States around the Appalachian range.

clue.text: Setter's wretched existence?

parts.note: surface reading: the crossword compiler grumbling about their miserable lot; setter's reading: a setter is a breed of gun dog, so this is the life of a hound

explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is usually the compiler, but here it is the sporting dog breed, whose life gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a miserable, harassed existence, the hard lot traditionally attributed to a mistreated hound.

clue.text: Takes in heroin and arsenic

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: Someone swallows a deadly cocktail of drugs and poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes in' reads as consuming the substances, but means deceives, as in 'you've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone is informal for to trick or fool them, the same sense as taking a person in.

clue.text: String quartet from Gossec or Dvorak?

indicators.note: a quartet is a set of four, taken from within the words that follow

parts.note: four letters running across the end of the first name, the little word and the start of the composer's surname

explanation.surface: A string quartet composed by one of two classical composers, Gossec or Dvořák.
explanation.walkthrough: 'String quartet' reads as a musical form; split it, and string is the definition while quartet says take four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is a thin rope or length of twine, a synonym of string.

clue.text: Mountain nymph backing appeal to Anglicans?

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the words that follow are read from the end

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of appeal or entreaty
CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A mountain spirit supports a plea to the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Echo was an oread, a nymph of the mountains, cursed to repeat only the last words of others.

clue.text: Island century or so ago banning travel

indicators.note: banning something keeps it out, so those letters are excluded from the word before

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century
taken as written
sic is Latin for so or thus
taken as written
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: An island where, about a hundred years back, journeys were forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Century or so ago' reads as a date, but 'or so' is split: or stays as written and so becomes the Latin SIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a large Mediterranean island belonging to France, the birthplace of Napoleon.

clue.text: Dangerous WWI agent really good with chat

parts.note: in British slang something mustard is excellent or very keen, as in keen as mustard
to gas is to talk idly or chatter

explanation.surface: A deadly First World War spy is excellent at small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' suggests a spy; here it is a chemical agent. Mustard as informal praise is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard gas is a blistering chemical weapon used in the trenches of the First World War.

clue.text: Butter club sandwiches in decorative craft?

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold something between two layers, so the second word goes round the first

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a ram is a butter, an animal that butts with its head

explanation.surface: A dairy spread and a club sandwich in some fancy cookery skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' and 'sandwiches' build a kitchen scene, but butter is one who butts, a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is the art of knotting cord or string into ornamental patterns, a decorative handicraft.

clue.text: Such a professional as might be called to account?

definitions.text: Such a professional as might be called to account?

parts.words: Such a professional as might be called to account?
parts.note: surface reading: a professional being held responsible and made to answer for failings; setter's reading: a professional summoned to go over the books of a business

explanation.walkthrough: 'Called to account' is an idiom for being blamed, but read literally it means summoned to examine the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional examines a company's financial records and checks they are accurate and fairly stated.

clue.text: Elgar is studied in African capital

indicators.note: studied can mean contrived or artificially arranged, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The English composer Elgar is on the syllabus at a North African conservatoire.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital city of Algeria, on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

clue.text: Copper tense after punch — that goes against the grain

indicators.note: after says the metal and the tense come behind the blow in the finished word

parts.note: a cross is a boxing punch thrown across the body
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous police officer, having been hit, is behaving in an irritating, contrary way.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; the definition is cryptic for a saw that cuts across wood fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosscut saw is designed to cut timber at right angles to the direction of its fibres.

clue.text: Tea's first, cereal second

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the drink word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A breakfast order: tea first, then a bowl of cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a position in the sequence, but it is a noun meaning a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice means in an instant, so a trice is a very short moment of time, like a second.

clue.text: Hold back time — the price?

parts.note: to dam is to hold back water
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: If you stop the clock, what will it cost you?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the damage?' is informal for 'how much do I owe?', which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the damage is the bill or cost of something, as in asking what the damage is.

clue.text: City revolutionary writer cripples?

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the words that follow are read the other way round

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as I
to maim is to cripple or injure badly

explanation.surface: Does a radical author disable people in some city?
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks as I, so 'writer cripples' gives I MAIM before it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a major city in Florida in the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Similar tit, cuckoo and hawk

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go mad and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of birds that look alike: a tit, a cuckoo and a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The three birds make a nature scene; only the last is the definition, in its political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk in politics favours aggressive military policy, the opposite of a dove, as does a militarist.

clue.text: Wife leaving got bigger cut

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter walks out of the word

parts.note: to wax is to grow larger, like the moon
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: After a wife walks out, someone earns a larger share.
explanation.definitionFit: Axed means chopped or, figuratively, cancelled or slashed, both senses of cut.

clue.text: Changes One put out by East European composer

indicators.note: putting something out ejects it, so that letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: varies means changes
the Roman numeral for one
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone shifts allegiance, ousted by an Eastern European composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East European' looks like one phrase, but East supplies a letter and only 'European composer' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was a French-born modernist composer, later based in America, known for pieces like Ionisation.

clue.text: Most ancient ateliers renovated

indicators.note: renovated means done up and remodelled, so the letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written; an atelier is an artist's studio

explanation.surface: The oldest artists' studios have been done up.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest things come first in time, so they are the oldest of a set.
